items.text: No single office runs the mortgage industry. A handful of federal bodies, plus every single state, each own a slice. Some protect the consumer, some insure or guarantee specific loan programs, one oversees the secondary market, and the states handle licensing on the ground. This is the overview — a later module takes each one in depth.

The main consumer regulator is the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau. Created after the two thousand eight crisis, the C-F-P-B writes and enforces most of the consumer-protection laws you'll deal with as an originator — the disclosure and fair-dealing rules that govern how a loan gets quoted, priced, and closed. If a rule is about how the borrower was treated, it's probably theirs.

A second cluster insures or guarantees particular kinds of loans. HUD — the Department of Housing and Urban Development — oversees housing and fair-lending programs, and the F-H-A, the Federal Housing Administration, operates inside HUD, insuring loans for lower-down-payment borrowers. The V-A, the Department of Veterans Affairs, guarantees loans for veterans and service members. The U-S-D-A guarantees loans for buyers in qualifying rural areas. None of these bodies police disclosures the way the C-F-P-B does. They make their loan programs possible by insuring or guaranteeing them. And watch those two verbs — F-H-A insures, V-A and U-S-D-A guarantee. The exam does not treat them as synonyms.

The F-H-F-A — the Federal Housing Finance Agency — oversees Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. And licensing, finally, happens at the state level. A state regulator issues and supervises your license, and does it through the N-M-L-S, the national system that tracks every originator across states and employers. Here's how much that matters in practice. Around a hundred and fifty-eight thousand people renewed an originator license in a recent year, and between them they held roughly five hundred sixty-eight thousand state licenses. Three and a half licenses each. One person, one exam, and then a separate license for every state they want to lend in. So: the F-H-F-A oversees the G-S-E-s. The states license the people.
